transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-01-24 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 mins | Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jade Lin (Redwood CSM), Samir Khan (VP Eng, Olive Tree), Priya Desai (Cloud Architect), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)

[00:00] Nina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:05] Samir: Yup, loud and clear. Thanks, Nina. We wanted to use this to align on the activation plan and make sure we don't miss any security hoops.
[00:10] Nina: Perfect — Jade and Marco from our side, Jade will run ops/runbook and Marco will handle technical bench and infra. Marco, quick intro?
[00:16] Marco: Hi all, Marco Ruiz — SE focused on runtime performance and private deployment patterns. I'll be doing the benchmark run and helping with VPC setup.
[00:22] Jade: Jade Lin, CSM. I'll schedule the weekly syncs and help unblock onboarding tasks.
[00:26] Priya: Priya here. I'm the cloud architect, will own the VPC and networking work.
[00:29] Liam: Liam, DevOps. I'll do the work with Peering and staging.

[02:10] Nina: Agenda — we have three big buckets: environment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance items (SAML, KMS, SOC 2), and pilot scope KPIs. We'll end with clear next steps.

[03:00] Samir: High-level context — our primary driver is confidentiality and predictable latency for certain credit-decision flows. We looked at Redwood's hosted API but we need VPC or on-prem because of auditors. Timeline wise, pilot in 6 weeks ideally.

[03:45] Marco: Got it. For predictable latency we usually recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated if you want managed reserved capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need customer-managed network. With your auditors needing isolation, VPC peering into Redwood Private is typical.

[04:30] Priya: When you say "Redwood Private" is that the private control plane or the on-prem appliance? We have constraints — no external egress of raw logs.

[04:45] Marco: Right, two modes: Private hosted in your VPC where control plane is customer-managed and we can configure KMS integration, or full on-prem package for air-gapped. For I/O, you can disable remote logs and push audit logs to your S3 bucket.

[06:12] Liam: Is there an expected egress IP list for peering? We need to set firewall rules.

[06:20] Marco: We'll provide a CIDR and host list for the staging cluster — but note IPs may change with autoscaling; best practice is to set up VPC peering and static NAT. We'll send the network diagram.

[07:05] Priya: Ok, also SSO — we use Okta. How does SAML integration look, RBAC, service accounts?

[07:18] Jade: We support SAML SSO via SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning if you want. You can map groups to roles via RBAC in the Console. We can also provision service principals for CI/CD.

[08:35] Samir: Auditors will ask about key management; we use AWS KMS CMKs. We need to make sure Redwood doesn't hold plaintext keys.

[08:45] Marco: KMS integration is supported — you can bring your keys (BYOK) and we can integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. We'll document the flow in the security pack.

[10:00] Priya: Data residency — some of the PII must stay in eu-west-1. Do you have region pinning?

[10:08] Nina: Yes, you can pin model serving to region. For the pilot we can run in eu-west staging. We'll note the region in the runbook.

[11:42] Liam: Pilot scope question — we want to run 3 credit decision prompts and a small batch 1k embeddings job. How do you recommend we size capacity?

[11:55] Marco: For short seq generation (<=256 tokens) the throughput on a single dedicated GPU for a 7B-ish model is X qps — (note: exact numbers depend on model/quant). We'll do a baseline run with your sample to recommend Dedicated pool size or suggest autoscale bursts.

[13:30] Samir: Cost sensitivity — we don't want open-ended spend during pilot. Can you set budgets/alerts?

[13:38] Jade: Yes, Console has token-level cost breakdown and budget alerts. We'll also put rate limits on the staging API keys.

[15:00] Priya: A couple of gotchas from infra — we use private subnets only, no public internet for instances. Will your agent require outbound?

[15:12] Marco: For the VPC-hosted variant, control plane connectivity requires limited outbound to the control endpoint; we can run a private connectivity path. For fully air-gapped we provide an appliance but that has an onboarding lead time.

[17:00] Samir: What's the typical lead time for the on-prem stack?

[17:07] Nina: On-prem delivery is longer — usually 6-8 weeks including compliance packaging. VPC peering into Redwood Private is faster — 1-2 weeks depending on your readiness. Since pilot is 6 weeks, VPC is a tighter fit but plausible.

[18:45] Priya: Can we do a hybrid — dev on hosted, pilot on VPC?

[18:53] Marco: Yes, that's common. We recommend dev on hosted for quick iteration, then migrate to VPC for pilot to satisfy auditors. We'll help automate model pinning and config so the same API calls work.

[21:30] Liam: Anything we should prepare for benchmarking? Sample prompts and representative request traces?

[21:38] Marco: Exactly. If you can share a few dozen representative prompts, average token lengths, and an example embeddings dataset we'll reproduce latency and cost numbers. Ideally a small dataset (2-5k rows) with a mix. Prefer sanitized PII-free samples — if PII exists mark it and we'll treat accordingly.

[23:00] Priya: On security docs — can you send SOC 2 attestation, penetration test summary?

[23:12] Jade: We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up (SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, network architecture doc). Expect that in an email by EOD tomorrow.

[25:05] Samir: Regarding model governance — we need model version pinning, rollback and evals. How do rollouts look?

[25:16] Marco: Console supports rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous variant. Redwood Optimize can also flag quality regressions tied to your eval sets. We'll show that in a follow-up demo if you want.

[26:30] Priya: Does the KV cache and batching affect determinism for our credit flow? We can't have cached prefixes cause different decisions unnoticed.

[26:40] Marco: Good point. We can disable prefix caching for sensitive endpoints, or enable strict cache invalidation policies. Batching is opt-in per route; for strict determinism you can set single-request routing. We'll document tradeoffs (latency vs cost).

[28:12] Liam: Ok. For telemetry, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is log export supported?

[28:20] Jade: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or pushed to your logging endpoint. We'll include the log schema and sample CloudTrail mapping.

[30:00] Samir: Risks — our biggest is audit timeline and ensuring no plaintext PII leaves our network. If we can get the security pack and VPC diagram early, we can unblock legal.

[30:15] Nina: We'll prioritize that; Jade will send the pack and Marco will start the bench plan.

[33:05] Marco: Quick note on benchmarking cadence — I'll do an initial dry run on our side with sample prompts, then run your sanitized set in staging. Expect a baseline report with latency percentiles (p50, p95), token cost estimates, and suggestions (quantization, batch windows).

[35:40] Priya: When will we get the staging credentials?

[35:47] Jade: After a short access form and signed NDA for the staging cluster. I'll share the link to the access checklist right after the call.

[37:10] Samir: Stakeholder check — our security lead wants to join the next meeting; can we add them?

[37:18] Nina: Absolutely, please add them. We'll keep next meeting as a 30-min technical checkpoint.

[39:00] Liam: One more — do you support customer-managed HSM?

[39:07] Marco: We support KMS BYOK and in some Private deployments support HSM integration; I'll validate specifics and call out any limitations in the security pack.

[41:20] Priya: About monitoring — do you expose traces and token-level metrics? We want to tie to our observability.

[41:30] Jade: Yes, per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and tracing hooks are available. We can connect metrics to your Datadog or Prometheus endpoints.

[43:05] Samir: Great. Sounds like a plan. Quick recap?

[43:15] Nina: Recap: 1) Marco will run bench with your samples and deliver report by 2026-01-29. 2) Jade will send onboarding runbook, access checklist, and security pack by 2026-01-26. 3) Samir will provide sample dataset + compliance list by 2026-01-27. 4) Set up a 30-min weekly technical sync starting next Tuesday.

[44:00] Priya: That matches our expectations. One ask — please include estimated monthly cost for pilot in the benchmark doc.

[44:10] Marco: Will do; include multiple sizing options.

[45:20] Nina: Any blockers?

[45:25] Samir: None immediate. We'll circulate NDA to Jade.

[46:45] Jade: I'll drop calendar invites for the weekly sync and include a link to the shared onboarding folder.

[47:30] Nina: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts. End call.
